examples.en: How is the host city of the Olympics decided?
The host of the next World Cup has been announced.
We changed the location of this conference to Busan.

examples.ko: 개최지에 따라 숙소 가격이 많이 달라져요.
examples.en: Accommodation prices vary a lot depending on the venue city.
I looked up how to get to the venue.
The city chosen as host is busy preparing.

explain: 올림픽, 월드컵, 학회, 박람회처럼 큰 행사가 열리는 도시나 지역을 가리켜요. 나라를 말할 때는 '개최국'이라고 해요. 작은 모임의 장소에는 '장소'를 더 자연스럽게 써요.

phrases.en: Busan was chosen as the venue for the next competition.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사를 열 도시가 결정되었다는 뜻으로 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news when the host city has been decided.
phrases.en_equiv: to be decided as the venue

phrases.en: The venue selection result comes out tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사 장소를 고르는 과정이나 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the process or result of choosing the host location.

phrases.en: Which country is hosting this World Cup?
phrases.nuance_en: '개최지' is a city or region, while '개최국' means the host country.

explain_en: It points to the city or region where a big event such as the Olympics, World Cup, academic conference or expo is held. When talking about the country, say '개최국'. For a small gathering, '장소' sounds more natural.

examples.en: The airport has so many passengers that the lines are long.

examples.ko: 이 배는 여객과 화물을 같이 실어요.
examples.en: This ship carries both passengers and cargo.
I went to Jeju Island on a passenger ferry.
The passenger terminal is in the city center.
The number of passengers rose compared with last year.
The passenger plane arrived later than scheduled.

explain: '승객'은 버스·택시·지하철까지 탄 사람을 두루 가리키는 일상어고, '여객'은 여객선·여객기·여객 터미널처럼 교통 사업이나 공항·항만 뉴스에서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 말할 때는 '승객'이 훨씬 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I went to Jeju Island on a passenger ship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 태우는 배를 말해요. '여객'이 들어간 가장 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A ship that carries people. The most common word containing 여객.

phrases.en: The passenger plane landed safely at the airport.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화물기와 달리 사람을 태우는 비행기예요. 뉴스에서 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plane that carries people, unlike a cargo plane. Often heard in the news.

phrases.en: I waited for my friend at the passenger terminal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공항이나 항구에서 사람이 타고 내리는 건물이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The building at an airport or port where people board and get off.

explain_en: '승객' is the everyday word for anyone riding a bus, taxi, or subway, while '여객' is a stiffer word used in transport business and airport or port news, as in '여객선', '여객기', '여객 터미널'. In speech, '승객' sounds much more natural.

examples.en: Commuting to school from so far was hard, so I moved.

examples.ko: 원거리 출퇴근 때문에 매일 두 시간씩 걸려요.
examples.en: My long commute takes two hours every day.

examples.ko: 이 버스에는 원거리 통학을 하는 학생이 많아요.
examples.en: Many students on this bus commute to school from far away.

examples.ko: 시력이 나빠서 원거리가 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: My eyesight is poor, so I can't see far things well.
We provide lodging for guests who come from far away.

examples.ko: 원거리 운전을 하기 전에 차를 점검했어요.
examples.en: I checked the car before the long drive.

explain: '원거리 통학', '원거리 출퇴근'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여 써요. 연애는 '원거리'보다 '장거리 연애'라고 더 자주 말해요. 반대말은 '근거리'이고, 일상에서는 그냥 '멀리'나 '먼 거리'라고 하는 때가 많아요.

phrases.example: 원거리 통학을 하면 아침에 일찍 일어나야 해요.
phrases.en: If you commute a long way to school, you have to get up early.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교가 멀어서 오래 다닐 때 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical pairing for traveling a long way to school.

phrases.en: It's a long way from home to work, so it's tiring.
phrases.nuance_en: A more natural phrase in everyday talk.

phrases.en: I tend to walk for short distances.

explain_en: It is usually followed by a noun, as in '원거리 통학' or '원거리 출퇴근'. For relationships, people more often say '장거리 연애' than 원거리. The opposite is 근거리, and in daily talk people often simply say '멀리' or '먼 거리'.

examples.ko: 안개 때문에 비행기 이착륙이 늦어지고 있어요.
examples.en: Take-offs and landings are being delayed because of fog.
The noise from take-offs and landings is bad near the airport.

examples.ko: 이착륙 때는 좌석 벨트를 꼭 매야 해요.
examples.en: You must keep your seat belt fastened during take-off and landing.
All take-offs and landings were canceled because of the typhoon.

examples.ko: 이 활주로는 하루에 이착륙이 백 번 넘어요.
examples.en: This runway handles over a hundred take-offs and landings a day.

examples.ko: 헬기 이착륙 장소가 학교 옆에 있어요.
examples.en: The helicopter landing pad is next to the school.

explain: '이륙'과 '착륙'을 한꺼번에 말하는 말이라 공항 안내나 뉴스에서 많이 나와요. 비행기뿐 아니라 헬기나 드론에도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The helicopter landing pad is on the rooftop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜨고 내리는 장소를 말할 때 '이착륙' 뒤에 '장'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 장 to 이착륙 names the place for take-off and landing.

phrases.example: 이착륙 시간에는 휴대폰을 비행기 모드로 해 주세요.
phrases.en: Please set your phone to airplane mode during takeoff and landing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기내 안내 방송에서 자주 듣는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often heard in in-flight announcements.

phrases.en: Takeoffs and landings were suspended because of strong winds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨나 사고로 비행이 멈췄다는 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in news about flights halted by weather or accidents.

explain_en: It bundles '이륙' (take-off) and '착륙' (landing) together, so it shows up in airport announcements and the news. It works for helicopters and drones as well as airplanes.

examples.en: The workers are unloading the cargo from the truck.
As soon as the ship arrived, they unloaded the containers.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 오늘은 짐을 하역할 수 없어요.
examples.en: It's raining, so we can't unload the cargo today.
I saw them unloading grain at the port.

examples.ko: 하역해야 할 화물이 아직 많이 남았어요.
examples.en: There is still a lot of cargo left to unload.

examples.ko: 크레인이 철강을 하역한 뒤에야 트럭이 움직였어요.
examples.en: The truck only moved after the crane had unloaded the steel.

explain: 실제로는 배나 차에서 짐을 '내리는' 장면에 가장 많이 써요. 짐을 싣는 쪽을 따로 말할 때는 '선적하다'나 '싣다'를 써요.

phrases.en: We are unloading the cargo from the ship right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 진행되고 있는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something happening right now.
phrases.en_equiv: to be in the middle of unloading

phrases.en: After unloading the cargo, the truck left.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 끝난 다음의 행동을 이어 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to link to what happens after the work is done.

phrases.nuance_ko: 작업 속도를 함께 말할 때 부사와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with adverbs to describe work speed.

explain_en: In practice it is most often used for unloading cargo from a ship or vehicle. To talk about the loading side separately, use '선적하다' or '싣다'.

examples.en: Check the train's destination before you board.
The destination is written on the front of the bus.

examples.ko: 그는 행선지도 말하지 않고 집을 나갔어요.
examples.en: He left the house without even saying where he was going.
We changed the destination and decided to go to Busan.
I told the taxi driver our destination.
The plane's destination suddenly changed.

explain: 행선지는 버스, 기차, 택시 같은 탈것이 가는 곳이나 누군가가 가는 곳을 말해요. 표지판에는 '행선지'가 쓰이고, 말할 때는 '어디 가요?'를 더 많이 말해요. 여행에서 목적으로 하는 곳을 말할 때는 '목적지'를 더 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I'll call you when I arrive at my destination.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가고 싶어서 정한 곳을 말해서, 탈것이 가는 곳을 뜻하는 행선지와 조금 달라요.
phrases.nuance_en: The place you decided to go; slightly different from 행선지, which is where a vehicle is headed.

phrases.en: I told the taxi driver my destination.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가는 곳을 다른 사람에게 알려 줄 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for telling someone where you are going.

phrases.nuance_ko: 행선지는 표지판에 쓰는 말이고, 말할 때는 이렇게 물어요.
phrases.nuance_en: 행선지 appears on signs; in speech people ask it this way.

explain_en: 행선지 is where a vehicle or a person is headed. It is written on signs, but in speech people just ask '어디 가요?'. For the place you aim for on a trip, '목적지' is used more often.
